facts.a: Source range: proportional counter. Intermediate range: compensated ion chamber. Power range: uncompensated ion chamber.

facts.q: How does a compensated ion chamber cancel gamma current?
facts.a: A boron coated chamber sees neutrons and gammas, an uncoated chamber sees gammas, and their currents are opposed.

facts.q: What does overcompensating a compensated ion chamber do?
facts.a: It blocks some neutron current too, so the meter reads low.

facts.q: What is the relationship between startup rate and reactor period?
facts.a: SUR = 26.06 / τ, with SUR in decades per minute and τ in seconds.

summary.text: Stopping power is proportional to specific ionization.
Alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation interact with matter in different ways.
Multiplication of electrons in a gas-filled detector is called gas amplification.
The alpha curve is higher than the beta curve from Region I to part of Region IV.
A compensated ion chamber sets its voltages so the gamma currents of the two chambers cancel.
The source range uses a proportional counter, the intermediate range a compensated ion chamber, and the power range an uncompensated ion chamber.
Gamma compensation is not required in the power range, since neutrons outnumber gammas by a large number.
